prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a sideswipe while changing lanes. The patient had 21 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1495; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred during a lane change, reporting right knee pain and swelling. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported force of the impact, and the pattern of symptoms matches what would be expected from this type of event. Over the course of 21 visits, care followed a conventional progression, beginning with rest, ice, and anti-inflammatory measures, then moving to supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and strengthening. Visit frequency decreased steadily as symptoms improved and function returned. Physical examination revealed localized tenderness and a limited range of motion, which support the reported injury, while several ligament stability tests and neurovascular checks returned normal results. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this knee. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated entries. At discharge, the patient was ambulating without assistance and was released to full activity with a home exercise program.
